text:
kevin: Quick heads up — I ran into conflicting wording in the Dedicated docs re: eviction / restart behavior. The provisioning page says pods are "auto-restarted" after eviction, but in our private Dedicated pools with strict isolation that isn't true. Causing a migration doc customer confusion.

maya: Which page/link?

kevin: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/blob/main/dedicated/provisioning.md#eviction-behavior — and the autoscale example shows `eviction: auto` in the YAML which feels misleading.

sre-anna: We never ``auto-restart`` workloads for pools marked `isolation: strict`. Nodes can be preempted and workloads may be rescheduled onto other nodes, but we do not perform a transparent restart in all cases. Need to call that out.

luca: To add context: runtime treats preemptible GPUs as "best-effort". Behavior depends on pool config + node group. For example, when `node_pool.preemptible: true` we drain and let k8s reschedule — that can appear as a restart from user perspective, but it's not guaranteed if there's capacity scarcity.

kevin: Here's the confusing snippet from the docs: 
```yaml
autoscale:
  policy: target_util
  target: 0.6
  eviction: auto  # current doc line
```

kevin: I think we should: 1) clarify "eviction" vs "preemption", 2) call out differences for `isolation: strict` vs `shared` pools, 3) add a migration note and an SDK snippet so customers can detect reschedules.

maya: Sounds good. I'll open a docs PR to separate those sections and add explicit examples + a migration checklist. Planning to put the migration checklist under dedicated/migration.md. Will link to runtime behaviour notes and include an SDK snippet to poll allocation state. I'll do PR #1873 today.

paul: I can add a tested example in the examples repo showing how to detect a reschedule and how to gracefully drain connection caches.

luca: For the SDK snippet, use the inference client to check `allocation.status` and `node_pool.preemptible` before starting long-lived sessions. Example we can include: 
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
alloc = client.get_allocation(allocation_id)
if alloc['node_pool']['preemptible']:
    # warn user, retry logic, shorter sessions
    print('Allocation on preemptible pool — use short-lived sessions')
```

maya: Nice. I'll paste that in the migration guide and add a sentence about SLA implications. Do we have SLA numbers we can include for preemptible vs reserved nodes?

sre-anna: We don't have a separate SLA for preemptible nodes. SLA applies to the Dedicated product level, but we should add a table showing expected availability delta when customers opt for preemptible pools or `isolation: best-effort`. I'll send numbers: nominal availability 99.9% reserved, ~99.0% with preemptible under heavy load (ballpark, will provide measured numbers).

kevin: Please also add a short "what to expect during autoscale" section — customers expect scaling to be instantaneous. Note that when adding nodes we have scheduling delays and potential temporary capacity shortfalls. Example checklist: scale-up timeout, retry logic for long-lived streams.

maya: Will do. Also found a dead link in the provisioning page to the SLA matrix: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/sla (404) — will fix to /dedicated/sla-matrix.md.

kevin: Great catch.

paul: Once PR is open, I can wire up an examples link and update the migration automation script in ops-samples repo.

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1873 — split sections, added SDK snippet and migration checklist, fixed SLA link, added placeholder for SLA table. PTAL.

deploy-bot: docs-ci: build succeeded for PR #1873 (:rocket:) — preview site: https://deploy.preview.redwood.ai/pr-1873/dedicated/provisioning.html

kevin: Quick review notes: reword first paragraph under "Eviction behavior" to avoid implying automatic restart. Also expand the SDK snippet to show polling loop backoff.

maya: Got it, pushing a small update now.

sre-anna: LGTM on wording change. Suggest adding footnote: "Strict isolation may result in manual intervention for rescheduling in regulated on-prem setups."

maya: Added footnote and the SLA table (numbers TBD by SRE). Updated PR.

kevin: Approving — thanks everyone. After SRE provides numbers we can merge and announce in #announcements with a short migration note.

maya: Will follow up for the announcement and add a short sample in the SDK docs. :thumbsup:
